problem: Prior methods for finding objects that humans move around (HOMER, SGM, OSG/CEG, TAP-LGX) predict discrete receptacle-level relations, need per-household training, scene graphs, hand-designed priors or costly VLM/LLM reasoning, and are evaluated in limited settings. They do not model continuous, multimodal future object locations that generalize across unseen homes.
motivation: Humans move objects following recurring routines, so a robot's last observation of an object is often stale. These routines create spatio-temporally consistent patterns that could be learned from data and exploited to direct search, without explicitly identifying the human activity. Because plausible placements are multimodal, a distribution over continuous 3D space is needed rather than a point estimate or a fixed label set.
key_idea: Train a latent conditional flow-matching model (VAE + conditional DiT) that samples future 3D bounding boxes of a queried object given the current scene map, the query label and the target time, and use clustered samples as ranked search targets for dynamic ObjectNav.
insight: Semantic conditioning is the dominant factor: in the ObjNav ablations, dropping the query class drops mSR from 65.86 to 43.33, and dropping scene class embeddings drops it to 55.52. Architectural pieces (scene encoder, structured bbox embedding) matter less, at roughly 4-6 mSR points. Multimodality is essential: collapsing samples to their centroid (MeanFlowMaps) is over 7x worse in minFDE. Failure analysis shows FlowMaps puts more successes in the first mode and has fewer step-budget failures, but more mode-exhaustion failures when the posterior misses the correct region.
method: Dynamic data generation: ProcTHOR scenes (2706 train / 918 val per habit) with up to 15 dynamic objects moving between compatible receptacles under three habit routines (favorite places / balanced / highly dynamic). Each scene is simulated for 4 weeks at hourly resolution (672 timestamps, >1.8M samples per habit); continuous placement uses potential-field sampling on receptacle surfaces. One model is trained per habit.

Object VAE: a residual-MLP VAE encodes each (normalized 3D bbox, class) token into a 32-d latent. It is trained with CIoU + L1 + CE + annealed KL, then frozen. Its decoder outputs the box and class logits.

Map encoder: scene tokens (bbox embedding via magnitude/direction MLPs, class, dynamic/static flag, observation-time embedding) go through an 8-layer permutation-invariant Transformer encoder with no positional encoding, producing context tokens H_tau (S=32).

CDiT flow network: 8 cross-attention DiT blocks refine the noisy query latent by cross-attending to H_tau. adaLN-Zero is conditioned on flow time, target time tau_f and query label. Per-block self-attention is removed because there is only one query token. A final head outputs the velocity in VAE latent space.

CFM training and sampling: CondOT straight-line path, Hungarian minibatch OT coupling, logit-normal time sampling, latents standardized. Inference uses Euler with step 0.05, one map-encoder pass amortized over queries and samples, then the VAE decoder outputs the box.
ObjNav integration: draw N_preds=25 samples, cluster with DBSCAN (eps 1 m, min 2), rank clusters by mass, and have the agent visit the cluster centroids in order using shortest-path navigation.

setting.backbone: Latent conditional DiT flow-matching (8 map-encoder layers + 8 CDiT blocks, width 256) + residual-MLP VAE, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Synthetic ProcTHOR dynamic-object trajectories: 2706 train environments per habit, 4 weeks hourly, >1.8M samples per habit; one model per habit
setting.observation: Symbolic scene map (3D axis-aligned bboxes + semantic labels of objects/receptacles) at observation time tau; ground-truth visibility in simulation; real robot uses a VLM only to trigger 'found'
setting.action_space: Ranked candidate target locations, navigated to with the AI2-THOR shortest-path planner (GetShortestPathToPoint) under a 1000-step budget
setting.privileged: Ground-truth object/receptacle bounding boxes as the map, ground-truth visibility for detection in simulation, and GT shortest-path distances

numbers_note: There is no standard benchmark; the ObjNav numbers are on the authors' own ProcTHOR dynamic-ObjNav minival. Success rates are given as SR@K in percent. The ablation table (avg over habits, full model: mSR 65.86, mSPL 46.66) is not listed as a separate row.
results: FlowMaps achieves the best mSR and mSPL on all three habits (69.26/48.95, 63.92/45.72, 64.39/45.30). Its SR@1 is 50-58%, well above the strongest baseline SGM (48.36 on Habit #1) and HOMER/Naive LLM on the others. On the distributional metrics it has the best minFDE (0.342 m, vs 0.370 for FreqPrior) and the best density and coverage. A real-robot TIAGo demo finds a phone at the second ranked target.
limitations: Closed vocabulary of 41 object classes and 17 receptacles, so it is not open-vocabulary
Requires large amounts of simulated training data, and a separate model is trained per habit; only three synthetic habits were evaluated
Failures are dominated by mode exhaustion when the posterior misses the correct region; perception relies on GT boxes and GT visibility in simulation
